_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). 30-round population-priority push, 2026-08-13 (AF/G.17). Sudan — highest-population country with zero prior corpus presence. Researched via a dispatched Agent (not sequential WebFetch), covering national CPI, COMESA membership, and provincial/state fiscal tier. War/insecurity materially affects two fields: CBS's own site is unreachable, and 2 of 18 states have field CPI collection replaced by estimates.

reports.title: Sudan Consumer Price Indices
reports.description: Sudan's national CPI, historically titled "Sudan Consumer Price Indices" (per a 2010 UNECE/ILO presentation quoting a COICOP-consistent 12-group structure). Current (2026) coverage confirmed via Sudan Tribune news reporting rather than CBS's own site (cbs.gov.sd is unreachable throughout this research round) — monthly, with 40-46% YoY inflation reported March/April 2026 and a basket described as "663 commodities... distributed across 12 categories." Two of Sudan's 18 states — Central Darfur (since April 2023) and North Darfur (since October 2025) — have had field price collection replaced by ESTIMATES due to the ongoing civil war, per the same reporting.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, per Sudan Tribune reporting on CBS releases; the primary CBS site is currently unreachable so this is confirmed only via secondary news coverage, not CBS's own bulletin.

reports.title: FY2026 Emergency Budget Guidelines — Council of Ministers Approval
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MoFEP), Sudan
reports.description: Sudan's Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning's own site, reporting the Council of Ministers' approval of the FY2026 emergency budget (approved December 2025, following an October 2025 guidelines/objectives approval). Verbatim (Arabic): "وتلتزم الموازنة بتحويل نصيب الولايات حسب قانون قسمة الموارد ووفق التحصيل الفعلي للإيرادات العامة في ظل عدم تحمل أي صرف إضافي" [The budget commits to transferring the states' share according to the Resource-Sharing Law and in accordance with the actual collection of general revenues, without incurring any additional expenditure]. This is MORE SPECIFIC than the aggregate lump-sum 'transfers to states' line already documented in sd-budget-2021-transfers: it names a specific governing law (the 'Resource-Sharing Law', قانون قسمة الموارد) and ties state transfers to actual revenue collection rather than a fixed figure — though the article itself does not quote the Resource-Sharing Law's own text or a formula/percentage. Deepens the national tier per this project's fallback rule (state-level fiscal transparency has collapsed under the war; the national tier is scoured instead).
reports.cadence_note: Annual budget approval; this is the FY2026 (emergency wartime) edition.

reports.title: Economic and Financial Statistical Review, Issue 1/2024 (October–December 2024)
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Sudan (Bank of Sudan / CBOS)
reports.description: Sudan's central bank publishes CPI/inflation data quarterly, sourced from CBS: Table No. (24), "Consumer Price Index & Inflation Rates / Base Year 2007=100 ... Source: Central Bureau of Statistics." Narrative: "The Inflation rate decreased from 215.5% by the end of September 2024 to 187.8% by the end December of 2024." Confirms CBOS continues to publish CPI-derived figures through the war period (this issue covers through Dec 2024), even though CBS's own website is unreachable and unresponsive throughout this branch's research. A full-text search of this 20-page document for COICOP, ILO, IMF, COMESA, or IGAD found no methodology-relevant mentions (one incidental, unrelated 'IMF (grant)' line in a balance-of-payments table).

reports.title: Sudan National Budget 2021 (Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, Sudan
reports.description: Sudan's 2021 national budget document (hosted by SIPRI). Table 17 shows an aggregate "Current transfers to the states" line (SDG 87.908 billion) and cites "Decree No. 504 of 2020" as the governing rule for state budgeting. This is an AGGREGATE national-to-states transfer figure, not a per-state breakdown — no individual Sudanese state's own budget document was found this round despite extensive search (state-level fiscal transparency appears to be essentially absent online, consistent with the ongoing conflict).

dependencies.basis: CBOS's own Table 24 explicitly attributes its published CPI/inflation figures to "Source: Central Bureau of Statistics" — the central bank republishes CBS's own index rather than compiling an independent one.

_dropped.edge: Red Sea State (Port Sudan) closing accounts, FY2024 -> a self-published state fiscal document
_dropped.why: A federal MoFEP article confirms Red Sea State submitted full closing accounts for FY2024 to the federal Chamber of Accounts ('سلمت ولاية البحر الأحمر حساباتها الختامية للعام المالي 2024م لديوان الحسابات...'), the single strongest evidence found of a still-functioning sub-national fiscal process during the war. But this is a federal article ABOUT the state's submission, not the state's own published document — the state's own finance-ministry domain (redseafinance.gov.sd) does not resolve. Genuine lead, not mintable as a standalone node this round.

_dropped.edge: Sudan Ministry of Foreign Affairs' own statement on the 2023-2025 IGAD suspension/withdrawal status
_dropped.why: News reporting (Shorouk News) attributes statements about IGAD ('a violation of Sudan's sovereignty... a dangerous precedent in the history of IGAD') to Sudan's Foreign Ministry, but no primary government document, press-release page, or verified statement transcript could be located (mfa.gov.sd's certificate has expired; sudan.gov.sd's own site search returned nothing on IGAD). Sudan's IGAD status remains reported only via secondary/news sources, not confirmed via a primary Sudanese government document.

Sudan's COMESA membership and the treaty's Article 140 statistical-harmonisation clause are both confirmed, but no document found this round has CBS's own CPI citing COMESA or the treaty directly — the connection is plausible but not documented. Left unlinked per the branch's evidence standard.

IGAD (Intergovernmental Authority on Development), the other major regional bloc Sudan belongs to, was searched for a statistical-harmonisation citation comparable to COMESA's Article 140 — none found this round.

Negative finding, recorded for future reference rather than as a dropped edge attempt: Sudan has NOT signed or ratified the African Charter on Statistics 2009 (an AU status table lists "48 Sudan - - -" with no signature/ratification dates), unlike many other African countries already wired to AU-level statistical instruments elsewhere in this corpus.

No individual Sudanese state's own budget or fiscal document was locatable this round (extensive search, explicitly failed) — the war has apparently collapsed most state-level online fiscal transparency. Best available substitutes used instead: the Interim National Constitution 2005 Art. 110 (general resource-allocation process, not independently re-verified against primary text this round) and a secondary IGC academic paper describing the National Revenue Fund / FFAMC (Fiscal and Financial Allocation and Monitoring Commission) and the 1971 People's Local Government Act — neither independently verified against primary legal text, so neither minted as a node this round. Flagged for a future session with more research budget to pursue Sudanese state fiscal law directly.
